title: Young and in business
paragraphs: Do you have a business brain? Are you always looking for the next great idea? Maybe, like me, you might feel that starting a new company is something you do later in life when you have more experience. But that's not always the case.

While some of us may feel young adulthood is a time of tentatively finding our place in the world, sleeping late and partying hard, others are already on a path to great business success. Take the founder of Microsoft, Bill Gates, who started his company as a young university student at Harvard in the US. There are many other examples of young entrepreneurs who have become hugely successful, proving that there's no minimum age to becoming top dog.

But to be the next business executive requires effort. You need to acquire a keen mind and good business acumen and above all, you need enthusiasm. Starting a new business comes with an element of risk but if you are able to spot the next big idea, it's probably worth giving it a try. Jessica Rose owns a jewellery making business and admits that "when I first started I had no business training whatsoever... but I kind of woke up one day and thought I'd really love to be a jewellery designer." She went on to be a successful young entrepreneur.

Being young and in business does have its drawbacks; you may worry you have nothing to bring to the table and that the people who work for you tend to be older and wiser. That's what young British entrepreneur Suleman Sacranie found. He started his third business whilst studying chemistry at university. He says "now I've got two additional directors who have grey hair" but when they first started he says he "could tell they were thinking in the back of their heads, 'I've got a kid sitting in front of me.'"

You may think setting up a new start-up is easier said than done. As well as ideas, you need financial backing and expert guidance. But if you're studying hard at university and don't have the desire to go into business and make your fortune, keep on studying — an education is priceless!

vocabulary.entry: business brain [n.] /ˈbɪznəs breɪn/ 商业头脑 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: She has a sharp business brain and makes good deals.
vocabulary.translation: 她有敏锐的商业头脑，能做成好交易。

vocabulary.entry: tentatively [adv.] /ˈtentətɪvli/ 试探性地；暂时地
vocabulary.example: He tentatively suggested a new approach.
vocabulary.translation: 他试探性地提出了一个新方法。

vocabulary.entry: entrepreneur [n.] /ˌɒntrəprəˈnɜː/ 企业家 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The entrepreneur built a global company from scratch.
vocabulary.translation: 这位企业家白手起家建立了一家全球性公司。

vocabulary.entry: top dog [n.] /tɒp dɒɡ/ 佼佼者；掌权者 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: He is the top dog in the industry.
vocabulary.translation: 他是这个行业的佼佼者。

vocabulary.entry: keen [adj.] /kiːn/ 敏锐的；渴望的
vocabulary.example: Dogs have a keen sense of smell.
vocabulary.translation: 狗有敏锐的嗅觉。

vocabulary.entry: business acumen [n.] /ˈbɪznəs əˈkjuːmən/ 商业头脑；商业敏锐度 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: His business acumen helped the company grow.
vocabulary.translation: 他的商业头脑帮助公司成长。

vocabulary.entry: spot [v.] /spɒt/ 发现；认出
vocabulary.example: She spotted a mistake in the report.
vocabulary.translation: 她发现了报告中的一个错误。

vocabulary.entry: bring to the table [phr.] /brɪŋ tə ðə ˈteɪbəl/ 提供；贡献 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Each team member brings unique skills to the table.
vocabulary.translation: 每位团队成员都贡献独特的技能。

vocabulary.entry: priceless [adj.] /ˈpraɪsləs/ 无价的；极贵重的
vocabulary.example: Friendship is priceless.
vocabulary.translation: 友谊是无价的。

vocabulary.entry: set up [phr.] /set ʌp/ 创办；建立 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: They set up a charity to help the homeless.
vocabulary.translation: 他们建立了一个慈善机构来帮助无家可归者。

vocabulary.entry: in the world [phr.] /ɪn ðə wɜːld/ 在世界上；到底 (强调)
vocabulary.example: Where in the world did you find that?
vocabulary.translation: 你到底在哪里找到那个的？

vocabulary.entry: acquire [v.] /əˈkwaɪə/ 获得；学到 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He acquired a taste for wine.
vocabulary.translation: 他养成了对葡萄酒的品味。

vocabulary.entry: above all [phr.] /əˈbʌv ɔːl/ 最重要的是 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Above all, stay calm in an emergency.
vocabulary.translation: 最重要的是，紧急情况下要保持冷静。

vocabulary.entry: come with [phr.] /kʌm wɪð/ 伴随；带有 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The job comes with many benefits.
vocabulary.translation: 这份工作附带许多福利。

vocabulary.entry: an element of [phr.] /ən ˈelɪmənt əv/ 有一点；有几分 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: There is an element of truth in what he said.
vocabulary.translation: 他说的有几分道理。

vocabulary.entry: give it a try [phr.] /ɡɪv ɪt ə traɪ/ 试一试 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: You might enjoy it – why not give it a try?
vocabulary.translation: 你可能会喜欢——为什么不试一试呢？

vocabulary.entry: whatsoever [adv.] /ˌwɒtsəʊˈevə/ 丝毫；任何 (用于否定句加强语气)
vocabulary.example: I have no doubt whatsoever.
vocabulary.translation: 我丝毫都不怀疑。

vocabulary.entry: go into business [phr.] /ɡəʊ ˈɪntə ˈbɪznəs/ 进入商业领域；经商 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: After university, he went into business with his brother.
vocabulary.translation: 大学毕业后，他和哥哥一起经商。

vocabulary.entry: make one's fortune [phr.] /meɪk wʌnz ˈfɔːtʃuːn/ 发财；致富 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: He went abroad to make his fortune.
vocabulary.translation: 他出国去发财了。

vocabulary.entry: keep on [phr.] /kiːp ɒn/ 继续；坚持 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Keep on trying and you will succeed.
vocabulary.translation: 继续尝试，你会成功的。
